_note: Judgements recorded by /prose:prose passes, so later passes stop re-litigating them.

_why.R33-taboo/loudly: Hop3's named doctrine (CLAUDE.md: 'Errors Are Never Silent - Fail Loud'). 'fail loudly' / 'aborts loudly' are terms of art here, not manner adverbs claiming a virtue.
_why.R29-synonym/client+user: In a client-server CLI these name two different things: the client is the program on the laptop, the user is the person typing. Both are needed in the same sentence.
_why.R34-verbless/labels: '**Case Study - <topic> (<date>)**:' and '**Fix:**' open a case or a remedy. Rule 34 exempts labels; the parser reads them as prose and mis-tags the imperative that follows.
_why.R9-hedge/work-to-Level: 'delegates that work to Level 2 LanguageToolchains': 'work' is a noun (the delegated work), not the hedge verb 'work to'. Parse artifact on en_core_web_sm.
_why.R34-verbless/inline-code+verb: 'Only the `LocalBuilder` delegates to LanguageToolchains': the verb 'delegates' is present; the parser loses it at the inline-code span. Parse artifact on en_core_web_sm.
_why.R34-verbless/list-question: 'What resources?' sits in a bullet list; rule 34 exempts list items. Same class: 'What package manager?', 'How to isolate?'.
_why.R34-verbless/docstring-fence: hook-specifications.md:390 fires inside a ```python fence nested in a ```` fence; the linter fails to mask the inner fence and reads the docstring as prose. The line is docstring prose, exempt under rule 34's fence exemption.
_why.R34-verbless/screenshot-alt: Rule 34 exempts figure captions; the parser reads consecutive markdown image lines '![alt](src)' as one prose sentence with no verb. The alt text is a caption, not a claim.
_why.R34-verbless/report-tagline: Experience-report series: the one-line app descriptor under the H1 ('Open source ERP and CRM for small and medium businesses.') is a subtitle, present verbatim-shaped in every sibling report (matomo, kanboard, gitea). A label, not a claim.
_why.R34-verbless/tr-title-label: reports/README.md: the bold '[TR-nn](...). <Full report title>' heading at the head of each entry is a label (link + verbatim report title), not a claim; the entry prose that follows carries the verbs.
_why.R34-verbless/report-section-lead: Experience-report series: each 'What this app exercised' section opens with a noun-phrase lead naming what the app tested ('An application that ships no installer CLI at all.'; matomo: 'An application with no user-creation CLI.'). House pattern across the 20 reports; the elaborating sentences that follow carry the verbs.
_why.R34-verbless/inline-code+verb-2: quickstart.md: '⚠️ The `-y` flag bypasses safety confirmations.': the verb 'bypasses' is present; the parser loses it at the inline-code span after the emoji. Same class as R34-verbless/inline-code+verb.
_why.R34-verbless/invoice-ninja-tagline: invoice-ninja.md:21 'Free open-source invoicing platform.': the series tagline under the H1, already allowed series-wide as R34-verbless/report-tagline. Recorded once under the app name so later passes stop re-reading it.
_why.R34-verbless/limesurvey-tagline: limesurvey.md:21 'Professional online survey and data collection tool.': the series tagline under the H1, same class as R34-verbless/report-tagline.
_why.R34-verbless/mattermost-tagline: mattermost.md:21 'Open source team collaboration platform.': the series tagline under the H1, same class as R34-verbless/report-tagline.
_why.R37-bold/invoice-ninja-why: invoice-ninja.md:37 carried a 66-char italic claim; rewritten in the 2026-07 pass, not exempted. Note for future passes: the sibling pattern 'declared `unsupported`' in Open sections is a plain negation, not a rule-7 foil.
_why.R34-verbless/paheko-tagline: paheko.md:21 'Nonprofit accounting and association management.': the series tagline under the H1, same class as R34-verbless/report-tagline.
_why.R34-verbless/vikunja-tagline: vikunja.md:21 'Open source task and project management.': the series tagline under the H1, same class as R34-verbless/report-tagline.
_why.R8-triad/hop3-fetch-guarantees: packaging-applications.md: the `hop3-fetch` paragraph's three-item enumeration (HTTP-error handling / transient-failure retries / sha256 verification) is a genuine enumerable list of distinct behaviours, not rule-8 cadence padding.
_why.R37-bold/milestone-status: results-links-2026-07.md: the italicised per-milestone status annotation after each ✅ heading ('**M1.1:** ... ✅: *status sentence*') is the file's standing field format, a label in summary position, not a bold punchline in running prose. Applies to every milestone line in this and sibling final-report files.
_why.R34-verbless/sm-verb-mistag: TR-01.md: en_core_web_sm tags the finite verbs 'provisions', 'ship', 'address' and 'summarises' as nouns (NNS/NN), so the conservative rule-34 test reports sentences that carry a main verb. Four allowlist entries recorded; transformer models would not fire.
_why.R31-runon/enumerated-foil-list: TR-01.md: '(i)/(ii)/(iii)' enumeration sentences and the catalogued application-mix sentence are enumerations or serial lists, not stitched distinct claims.
_why.R12-inflated/next-generation-internet: README.md:270 'Next Generation Internet' is the NGI programme's name, linked to ngi.eu, in the funding statement. Only the spaced form is allowed; the marketing adjective 'next-generation' is hyphenated and still fires.
_why.R8-triad/tier3-label: TR-01.md 5.3: 'prebuilt-archive or prebuilt-binary' names the two Tier-3 template names; a genuine enumeration, already allowlisted.
_why.R34-verbless/reference-entries: TR-01.md §9 References: each '[n] Author. "Title." Venue, year.' entry is a verbatim bibliographic record, not a claim; rule 34's running-prose scope does not extend to reference lists. Covers lines 354-376 (Borg/Omega, Dolstra, NixOS, Unikraft, Pluggy) and the PhD thesis line.
_why.R37-bold/reference-venue: TR-01.md §9: italicised venue names (*Proc. 13th ACM SIGPLAN ICFP*, *Proc. 16th EuroSys*) are citation formatting, not bold punchlines.
_why.R31-runon/template-pattern-list: TR-01.md 3.5: the 58-word sentence ends in an eight-item serial enumeration of template patterns; rule 31's list exemption applies and splitting would hide that the list is the subject's predicate.
_why.R29-synonym/document-root: TR-01.md 4.2: 'a fixed document root' is the nginx term (the web server's root directory), not a synonym rotation with 'deployer'/'file'. False positive on 'document'.
_why.R34-verbless/privacy-data-list: privacy-policy.md: '- Browser, operating system and device type.' sits in the bullet list of data Umami collects; rule 34 exempts list items, and a bare enumeration of data categories is the correct shape there.
_why.R30-frozen/code-of-conduct: privacy-policy.md: 'Code of Conduct violation' is the policy document's proper name; 'conduct' is the noun of the title, not a nominalised verb.
_why.R34-verbless/link-definitions: CHANGES.md ends with a block of markdown link-reference definitions ('[0.7.4]: https://github.com/.../compare/...'). They are link syntax, not running prose; the parser reads the run of them as one verbless sentence. Same class as rule 34's exemption for labels and table cells.
_why.R34-verbless/html-image: README.md opens and closes with raw '' tags (the logo, the REUSE badge). Image markup, not running prose; rule 34 exempts captions and labels for the same reason.
_why.R31semi/letscode-tool-list: README.md:284 lists three tool groups whose items carry their own commas, so semicolons are the correct separator. Rule 31 names this exact case as its exemption and reports it as 'inspect'.
_why.R27-aphorism/url-tails-NOT-allowed: NOT exempted, recorded so the next pass does not chase it: the rule-27 count on README.md is a false positive. The sentence splitter breaks markdown link targets at the dot, so 'https://hop3.cloud/get-started/installer/).' becomes a short final 'sentence' with no digit and trips the aphorism test. Seven of the eight counted closers are URL tails, one is a list lead-in ('The stack includes:'). The fix belongs in the linter's masking, not in the prose. Do not silence it with a ')' pattern, which would blind rule 27 across the project.
_why.R34-verbless/principle-implementation: core-values.md pairs '- **Principle**: …' with '- **Implementation**: …' under each numbered security heading. They are nested list items, which rule 34 exempts; the linter does not read a bullet indented under an ordered item as a list item, so all twenty fired. The label-value shape is the point of the section and rewriting them into sentences would lose the parallel.
_why.R31-runon/threat-model-scope-lists: security-model.md:49,51 are the threat model's 'In scope:' / 'Out of scope:' enumerations. Each item carries its own commas, so semicolons are the correct separator and the count (5 and 8) is list length, not stitching. Rule 31 names this case as its exemption and reports it as 'inspect'.
_why.R34-verbless/nested-fence-leak: external-plugins.md:356,400 and hook-specifications.md:393 are code-fence CONTENT, reported as prose. The masker toggles on any line starting with ``` and ignores fence length, so a nested example desyncs it and everything after leaks. external-plugins.md's outer README example was widened to four backticks in this pass, which is what CommonMark requires and fixes the rendering; the masker still desyncs because it does not compare fence lengths. Reported upstream.
_why.R34-verbless/bullet-character: notes/ngi-2024/annex.md lists milestones as '• M2.1 …' with U+2022, not '-'. The linter reads only '-'/'*' as list markers, so each run of bullets is parsed as one verbless sentence. Rule 34 exempts list items. The annex is the contractual Annexe I submitted to NLnet; its wording is not ours to edit for style.
_why.R34-verbless/report-front-matter: results-links-2026-*.md open with 'Status: … / Date: …' label lines and a one-line scope note under the H1. Front matter and a caption, not running prose. The 06 report is marked final and was submitted; it is a record of what was sent and is not edited for style.
_why.R3-foil/table-header-row: release-plan-0.6.md:16 is a markdown table header, '| Milestone | 0.5 Status | 0.6 Outcome |'. The nlp foil detector matches across the pipe delimiters. A table row is not prose.
_why.R8-triad/two-item-condition: release-plan-0.7.md:93 'an empty or non-zero recording' is a two-branch failure condition, not a triad assembled for cadence.
_why.R31-runon/checklist-headers: release-plan-0.7.md:160,170 are italic headers introducing checkbox lists ('*Ships in 0.7, supported (experimental):*'); the semicolons counted belong to the list items merged in after them. Same class as the threat-model scope lists.
_why.R34-verbless/annex-deliverable-text: annex.md:51 'Package 20 popular or useful open-source applications…' is the T4 deliverable description, an imperative the parser reads as a noun. It is contractual text from Annexe I as submitted to NLnet, so it is not rewritten for style.
_why.R31-runon/submitted-final-report: results-links-2026-06.md:6 is a serial list whose items carry their own commas (docs links; code on SourceHut; ADRs), which rule 31 exempts. The report is also marked 'Status: final' and was submitted; it records what was sent.
_why.R1-emdash/table-no-data-cell: NOT exempted, deliberately: TR-03's results tables use '—' in a cell to mean 'no measurement' (461, 463, 527, 616-620), the standard scientific-table convention, not a prose incise. The snippet is the bare character, so the only pattern that would silence it is '—', which would disable rule 1 project-wide. Left visible; the fix belongs in the linter, which should mask markdown table rows as it masks fenced code.
_why.R34-verbless/section-sign-subject: TR-03:369 '§7.4 states where each claim's replication stops.' has the verb 'states'; the tokenizer mis-reads '§7.4' and the verb becomes a noun. The paper uses § 166 times, so respelling one of them for the parser would break its own convention.
_why.R34-verbless/past-tense-read-as-particip: TR-03:439 'Four applications in this corpus rebuilt deterministically while failing to start' — 'rebuilt' is the finite past tense, read as a participle.
_why.R34-verbless/table-and-figure-captions: TR-03:465 is a '*Table 6: …*' caption and :704 a markdown image with alt text. Rule 34 exempts captions.
_why.R29-synonym/distinct-referents-tr03: TR-03's three rotation hits name different things: 'a small business' and 'an organisation' are separate example actors in one enumeration of who needs sovereignty; 'the decision record' and the 'lessons-learned notes' are two artefacts, with 'file' naming files inside them; 'a codebase' is generic (what codaviz explores) while 'the repository' is Hop3's own.
_why.R30-frozen/make-X-executable: TR-03:698 '`validoc` makes documentation executable' is a resultative (make + object + adjective), not a light verb in front of a nominalisation. There is no verb the sentence is avoiding.
_why.R37-bold/term-being-coined: TR-03:85 italicises '*dependency-level reproducibility without OS-level virtualisation*' at the point it names the paper's fourth path, right after 'A fourth path is available:'. A term being defined, which rule 37 exempts as a label.
_why.R31-runon/tr03-lists-and-arguments: NOT exempted by pattern, recorded as a standing judgement: TR-03's twenty rule-31 hits were each read in this pass and none is a stitch. Thirteen are serial lists whose items carry their own commas — enumerated requirements '(i) …; (ii) …', the five credential defects, the deploy-time figures per strategy — which rule 31 names as its exemption. The rest are single arguments developed through subordination, which rule 31 says are fine and which splitting would damage: the verification-bar progression at :804 and the closure-size comparison at :512 are the clearest. Re-read them if the text changes; do not split them on the count alone.
_why.R12-inflated/elevated-privilege: ADR 041 uses 'elevated privileges' / 'elevated capabilities' in the security sense (privilege elevation), which is the field's term. Rule 12 targets the marketing register (leverage, seamless, robust-as-compliment).
_why.R9-hedge/work-to-noun: ADR 041:16 'pushed root-needing work to install time' and :86 'copying the work to two more proxy plugins'. 'work' is the noun, not the hedging verb 'work to'. Same parse artifact as the recorded work-to-Level case.
_why.R34-verbless/verb-read-as-noun: ADR 041:204 'Common fields map 1:1 (…)' — 'map' is the finite verb, read as a noun after a plural subject. :720 'The error-code taxonomy is unchanged: `ProxyError` / …' has 'is'; the masked code spans after the colon leave the parser nothing to attach.
_why.R37-bold/named-threat-model: ADR 041:60 bolds 'hop3-server compromise = total compromise' at the point it names the threat model ('The threat model is therefore named explicitly:'). A coined label, which rule 37 exempts.
_why.R3-foil/rejected-because-list: ADR 041:768 the nlp foil detector fires inside an alternatives entry, '**Rejected** because: heavy dependency (polkit not always present on minimal systemd setups); …'. A reasons list, not a balanced foil.
_why.R31-runon/adr041-alternatives-and-lists: NOT exempted by pattern, recorded as a judgement: ADR 041's nine rule-31 hits were read in this pass. Most are the 'Considered alternatives' entries, whose form is '**Rejected** because: reason; reason; reason' — serial lists whose items carry their own commas, which rule 31 names as its exemption and which is the ADR genre's own shape. The rest (the three-layer threat model at :200, the drift causes at :275, the reconciliation consequences at :281) are single arguments developed through subordination. Re-read if the text changes; do not split on the count.
_why.R3-foil/table-separator-row: ADR 043:54 is a markdown table's '|-------|----------|' separator row; the nlp foil detector matches across the dashes. Also seen on release-plan-0.6.md's header row. A table is not prose.
_why.R3-foil/plain-negation-in-adr: ADR 045:35 'conflict detection is DB-based and does not need rootd' and ADR 049:98 'no signed timestamp/TTL, so a NAT'd node can sit on old-but-valid content' are plain factual negations, which rule 3 explicitly leaves alone, not balanced foils.
_why.R34-verbless/adr-verb-present: Eight sentences across ADRs 042, 045, 046, 047 and 048 carry their finite verb (seeds, has, are baked, routes, require, errors, are, resolves) and are reported verbless anyway: each has an inline-code span or a § reference between the subject and the verb, or a long parenthetical, and the masker blanks it to whitespace so the parse loses the head.
_why.R37-bold/quoted-project-ethos: ADR 044:13 italicises the project ethos as quoted from CLAUDE.md: '*packaging apps is system-validation work; each app is a deliberate probe of the platform's edges.*' Rule 37 exempts quotations set in italics, and an invariant forbids editing quoted material.
_why.R35-coordination/adr043-enumerations: NOT exempted: ADR 043's three remaining hits are a three-item list sharing one verb ('the README, `CLAUDE.md`, and the Makefile call them'), a second such list, and a relative clause ('which every release accepts, and the current deployer keeps as aliases'). The sheet names enumerations and relatives as NOT this rule. Three rewrites were tried in this pass and each read worse than the original, which was restored.
_why.R27-aphorism/short-factual-closers: NOT exempted: ADR 048 reports 5 of 8 paragraphs closing on a 'short generalisation'. Two are masking artifacts ('`hop3-server.toml` carries no secret.' loses its subject to the mask, leaving three words); the other three are short factual statements ('No separate salt is provisioned by default.'), which is how technical paragraphs end. With 8 eligible paragraphs the 33% ceiling allows two. Padding factual closers to clear a rate would be the wrong trade.
_why.R34-verbless/adr05x-verb-present: Five sentences across ADRs 050, 051, 052 and 054 carry their finite verb (commits, is, recur, takes, is) and are reported verbless: each has a long parenthetical, an inline-code run, or a masked quotation between the subject and the verb, and the masker blanks it to whitespace.
_why.R37-bold/adr052-labels: ADR 052:20 italicises a parenthetical enumeration of the concepts the ADR is about ('*which server, where to install from, which optional services, how loud, machine-readable?*'), and :119 bolds the precedence formula 'explicit flag > env var > built-in default'. Both are labels, which rule 37 exempts; neither is a sentence set as a punchline.
_why.R31-runon/adr05x-enumerations: NOT exempted, recorded as a judgement: the fifteen rule-31 hits across ADRs 050-058 were read in this pass. They are the genre's own shapes — '**Positive**: …; …; …' and '**Negative**: …; …; …' consequence lists, the per-request evaluation order '(1) …; (2) …; (3) …', and the flag-inventory comparisons in 052 that list each tool's options. Every one is a serial list whose items carry their own commas, which rule 31 names as its exemption. Re-read if the text changes; do not split on the count.
_why.R31-runon/adr060-three-ways-list: NOT exempted, recorded as a judgement: ADR 060:53 'Three ways to empty a bucket were available: keep `mc`, which …, so …; add `boto3`, roughly 15 MB …; or sign the two required S3 requests directly.' is a serial list whose items carry their own commas, which rule 31 names as its exemption.
_why.R34-verbless/report-taglines-and-leads-b: The remaining experience-report taglines (bugsink, isso, keycloak, miniflux, radicale) and 'What this app exercised' leads (bugsink, invoice-ninja, isso, paheko, vikunja), recorded one pattern each under the series judgements R34-verbless/report-tagline and R34-verbless/report-section-lead.
_why.R31-runon/ngi-funding-statement: README.md: the NLnet / NGI0 Commons Fund acknowledgement is the funder's standard wording (fund, programme, DG CONNECT, grant agreement number), reproduced as funded projects are asked to. Not ours to split for style; same class as R12-inflated/next-generation-internet.
